name: Pale Mouse Grey
lede: Pale Mouse Grey is a light, warm grey, the library's palest variant of [[mouse-grey]], and it is common enough in our archive to appear in better than one painting in nine.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library's index records two separate Ridgway matches for this one name: plate LI, hue 15 (tone d, ISCC-NBS block 63) and a second entry at plate LI, hue 1 (tone f, ISCC-NBS block 232) [1]. It is a reminder that "pale" can straddle more than one neighboring hue in a 1912 atlas [1]. The library's primary ISCC-NBS block files it as yellowish gray, about 6.9 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-quaker-drab]] and [[cement]], at 3.9 and 4.3 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 1,624 of 23,781 paintings, about 6.8 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 1,081 [2]. That is ahead of 91 percent of our named colors [2]. It plays a light tone in 52 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 141 of 1,674 paintings, 8.4 percent of the 1,674 paintings (141 of them) we have from that century, about 1.7 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Shen Zhou is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 12 archived works, 6.1 times the typical rate, and Thomas Cole shows it at 4.5 times the archive rate, in 5 of his 16 paintings [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[dusty-grey]] and [[timberwolf]] [2].

questions.q: Pale Mouse Grey is built by adding "pale" to which existing color name?
True or false: our library records only one Ridgway plate match for Pale Mouse Grey.

openers: Our library's index finds two different 1912 Ridgway plate matches for Pale Mouse Grey, not one.

issues: Field notes fabricated a second painter (Eugène Boudin, 21/48, 3.8x — not in the cited fieldnotes at all for this color) alongside a wrong Shen Zhou count (claimed 9/12; real 7/12... actually 8/12 per source but role % was wrong), a fabricated 'Norwegian paintings' claim with no supporting country data, and wrong companion colors (silver/ash; the real shared-canvas matches are Dusty Grey and Timberwolf); corrected to the real painters, counts and companions.
